records.expectedPreparationMethod: Clean leaves and stems are boiled in water to prepare an external decoction for skin wash, or crushed fresh into a topical emollient poultice. Not formulated for internal medicinal ingestion.
records.preparationMethod: Reported traditional preparation: a decoction of Abutilon indicum leaves used externally as a wash. StuartXchange documents this Philippine practice but does not specify quantities or boiling time for that use. This is an ethnobotanical description, not a clinically validated treatment recipe.

source.title: StuartXchange Philippine Medicinal Plants: Malbas / Abutilon indicum
source.citation: Folkloric uses section reports a Philippine external leaf-decoction wash. It does not specify stems, crushed-leaf poultice preparation, quantities or boiling time for that wash. Traditional documentation is not clinical safety or efficacy validation.

records.expectedPreparationMethod: Fresh aromatic leaves are crushed and steeped in hot water for 5 to 10 minutes to brew an herbal infusion.
records.preparationMethod: The historical book mentions an infusion in a shared account of three basil species and a leaf decoction specifically for Ocimum gratissimum. It gives no measured, species-specific household recipe or steeping time. These descriptions are historical records, not a validated treatment guide.

source.title: The Medicinal Plants of the Philippines (1901)
source.citation: Mint Family, pages 195-196: the infusion account groups three basil species; the leaf-decoction report specifically names O. gratissimum. No species-specific measured infusion recipe or steeping time is supplied in this passage. Historical reports do not establish current clinical efficacy or safe household treatment.
